worry_scenarios.description: English pre-sleep worry scenarios. Each scenario = typical worry content + emotion keywords + intensity range + matched CBT-I technique recommendations. Helps the AI identify the worry type and select the right intervention.

typical_worries: Tense relationship with manager or coworkers
Career decisions or future direction unclear
Still thinking about work after hours
Made a mistake at work, afraid it'll be discovered
emotion_keywords: more I try the more awake I am

recommended_techniques.rationale: Work worry often co-occurs with sleep-effort syndrome — the harder you try, the more awake you get. Paradoxical intention targets that cycle directly.

example_prompts: Can't stop thinking about work tomorrow
Worried I messed up — my boss is going to find out
Can't sleep, my head is full of tomorrow's stuff

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about exams and academic life.
typical_worries: Behind on review, too much material
Don't know if studied the right things

recommended_techniques.rationale: Exam worry often pairs with mid-night rumination. Education that sleep consolidates memory reduces the 'I should review more' loop.

example_prompts: I have an exam tomorrow and I'm panicking
Can't sleep, just kept reviewing in my head
What if I fail this one

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about friends, coworkers, and social situations.
typical_worries: Conflict or misunderstanding with a friend / coworker
Said something I'm replaying over and over
Feeling left out of a group
Worried someone is upset with me
emotion_keywords: did I say the wrong thing

recommended_techniques.rationale: Social rumination is best interrupted by loving-kindness (sends warmth instead of replay) plus a gentle rumination_break closure.

example_prompts: Can't stop replaying what I said to my friend
I think they're mad at me
Why did I say that, it keeps coming back

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about physical health or body symptoms.
typical_worries: Afraid to make a doctor's appointment

recommended_techniques.rationale: Health anxiety has strong somatic activation. Down-regulating arousal first (4-7-8) before any cognitive work.

example_prompts: Keep feeling this in my chest and I can't stop worrying
What if the test results are bad
I'm scared something is really wrong

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about life direction, decisions, and uncertainty.
typical_worries: Don't know what to do with my life
Big decision pending — stay or leave
emotion_keywords: everyone else seems to have it figured out

recommended_techniques.rationale: Existential worry rarely has a 3 AM answer. Open awareness teaches that not every thought needs an answer right now.

example_prompts: Don't know what I'm doing with my life
Should I take this job or not — keep going in circles
Everyone else seems sorted, I'm just lost
clue_phrases: what to do with my life

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about money, debt, or financial security.
typical_worries: Bills piling up, not enough income
emotion_keywords: what if I lose my job

recommended_techniques.rationale: Money worry triggers strong fortune-telling. Reframing 'tomorrow's calculations need a rested mind' helps reduce nighttime ruminating.

example_prompts: Can't sleep, money is so tight this month
What if I lose my job, how would I pay rent
Keep doing the math in my head

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about family, parenting, or caring for others.
typical_worries: Worried about a child's behavior / school / health
Aging parents' health or care decisions

recommended_techniques.rationale: Parental / caregiving worry is often loaded with 'I should' rules. Loving-kindness (especially toward oneself) softens self-criticism; cognitive work targets should-statements.

example_prompts: Worried sick about my kid
I feel like a terrible parent tonight
Mom's health has me up at 3 AM

scenarios.description: Pre-sleep worries about a romantic partner, breakup, or relationship status.
typical_worries: Going through a breakup or divorce
Single and worried about being alone

recommended_techniques.rationale: Romantic rumination loops hard. Loving-kindness (toward self AND the other) plus a rumination_break interrupts late-night replay.

example_prompts: Had a fight with my partner and can't sleep
Keep replaying what they said
What if this is the end of us
